elon-musk:
## January 2025: DOGE scrutiny and the Bannon feud

As [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s inauguration approached, Musk drew intensified media fire over the [[doge|Department of Government Efficiency]], the advisory panel he was tapped to oversee with [[vivek-ramaswamy|Vivek Ramaswamy]] and which was charged with identifying $2 trillion in federal budget cuts.[n] MSNBC argued the pair had no background in auditing or the federal budget and that the panel had no actual power beyond issuing memos.[n] [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] of [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] countered that power in a transformational change effort is asymmetrical, invoking [[the-starfish-and-the-spider|The Starfish and the Spider]] to argue that the idea of DOGE — ending waste, fraud, and abuse — was itself what made Musk powerful, whatever his formal authority.[n]

At the same time, [[steve-bannon|Steve Bannon]] publicly taunted Musk in remarks to Politico, saying the president-elect's billionaire right-hand man had influence over Cabinet picks and policy discussions but did not "have the ability to actually make decisions and inform those decisions and drive those decisions."[n] Bannon pointed to [[scott-bessent|Scott Bessent]] winning the Treasury nomination over Musk's favorite, [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]], and to the fight over H-1B visas as evidence of the limits on Musk's sway.[n] Separately, Musk took fire from the gaming community he had courted over allegations that he faked his skill at Path of Exile 2; [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] of Badlands Media treated the episode as part of a "war of stories," observing that Musk, like "The Donald," is partly an invented character — and that this was not necessarily a bad thing.[n]
steve-bannon:
## January 2025 feud with Elon Musk

On January 14, 2025, Bannon taunted his fellow [[donald-trump|Trump]] ally [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]], telling Politico White House bureau chief Dasha Burns that the president-elect's billionaire right-hand man did not have all that much power.[n] Bannon, a former chief strategist for Trump and host of the "War Room" podcast, allowed that Musk had exercised some influence over Cabinet picks and policy discussions but said he did not "have the ability to actually make decisions and inform those decisions and drive those decisions."[n]

Politico framed the exchange as a prime example of the infighting already underway as Trump's big-tent GOP returned to power, with allies arguing it reflected a governing style in which Trump retains decision-making power while ensuring no single faction gains too much control.[n] In dismissing Musk's influence, Bannon pointed to [[scott-bessent|Scott Bessent]] prevailing over Musk's favorite [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]] for Treasury secretary, and to the fight over H-1B visas, which he predicted would push Musk closer to the MAGA loyalist position that the program should be abolished entirely.[n]
robert-f-kennedy-jr:
## Supreme Court denial of the Children's Health Defense COVID appeal (January 2025)

On Monday, January 13, 2025, the [[supreme-court-of-the-united-states|Supreme Court]] blocked Kennedy's [[childrens-health-defense|Children's Health Defense]] from stopping investigations of doctors in Washington state over possible COVID-19 misinformation.[n] The ruling came after Justice [[elena-kagan|Elena Kagan]] had denied the bid in November; Kennedy's group and the doctors then asked Justice [[clarence-thomas|Clarence Thomas]] to review their application for an injunction pending appeal, and Thomas referred the matter to the full court.[n] None of the justices noted any disagreement with the denial.[n] Kennedy, then President-elect [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s nominee to lead the Department of Health and Human Services, had founded CHD, which joined other plaintiffs in arguing that investigations seeking to sanction doctors for their views on COVID would violate free speech rights under the First Amendment.[n]
gavin-newsom:
## January 2025 California wildfires

As California burned in January 2025, Newsom sat for a half-hour podcast interview with former Obama administration official Jon Favreau, drawing sharp criticism from The Federalist, which wrote that "if excuses were good for putting out fires" the governor could have fixed his state in a jiffy.[n] In the interview Newsom characterized every criticism leveled at him as "misinformation," described himself as just as much a victim as anyone who watched their home burn, and maintained that he was helping fix the problem even though it was not his responsibility.[n] When Favreau suggested Newsom was "ultimately responsible as the governor of the state" and that a newly announced investigation into a water shortage looked to some like an effort to pass the blame, Newsom rejected the framing, saying, "I've got that question… And I want to get the answers."[n]
mohammed-bin-salman:
## January 2025 call with Brazil's president

On Monday, January 13, 2025, the Saudi Crown Prince received a phone call from [[luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva|Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva]], the Saudi Press Agency reported.[n] The two leaders reviewed the strong relations between [[saudi-arabia|Saudi Arabia]] and [[brazil|Brazil]] and emphasized their commitment to further developing cooperation across various fields, discussing topics of mutual interest and reaffirming a shared vision for addressing global and regional challenges.[n]

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] of [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] linked the outreach to Saudi Arabia's successful pilot program for extracting lithium from oil-field brine, funded by [[saudi-aramco|Aramco]] and the national mining company [[maaden|Ma'aden]], noting Brazil's standing as the ninth largest oil supplier in the world in 2022.[n] He noted that Saudi Arabia had been invited to join [[brics|BRICS]] but had delayed entry for unspecified reasons, which he suspected was tied to keeping the US dollar propped up as a favor to President [[donald-trump|Trump]], and argued that if MBS shares the lithium technology widely it would let many players enter the lithium market and prevent another OPEC-style energy oligarchy from dominating the world economy.[n]
joni-ernst:
## Role in the Hegseth confirmation hearing (January 2025)

Ernst, a veteran and sexual assault survivor, was widely seen as a key Republican vote on the Senate Armed Services Committee and critical to the confirmation chances of [[pete-hegseth|Pete Hegseth]] as defense secretary.[n] At the January 14, 2025 hearing she appeared satisfied with Hegseth's responses to her questions about the role of women in the military and about sexual assault prevention, and spent much of her allotted time focusing on an area of agreement between them: that the [[pentagon|Pentagon]] should be audited.[n] Her posture helped Hegseth emerge from the more than four-hour hearing with Republican support intact.[n]
